Passage needed guides, witnesses and route holders; river travel remained seasonal.

Dorohychyn's routes, crossings and local power affected dealings between Rus and western neighbors. Danylo's struggle for control concerned military passage as well as protection and dues for residents, goods and envoys. A crossing could separate the advance party from baggage, requiring escorts to watch both banks and the remaining column. Urgency could not replace boats or workable water.

Dorohychyn's routes, crossings and local power affected dealings between Rus and western neighbors. Danylo's struggle for control concerned military passage as well as protection and dues for residents, goods and envoys. Controlling a crossing offered income and influence but required guards, boats and repair. Requisitioning boatmen interrupted their livelihood and needed arrangements for provisions and return.

Dorohychyn's routes, crossings and local power affected dealings between Rus and western neighbors. Danylo's struggle for control concerned military passage as well as protection and dues for residents, goods and envoys. Households crossing for markets, kin or livestock faced waiting and fares. A blocked passage meant longer travel, more food and lost fieldwork.
